road.title: Finding the way
road.description: A long-limbed figure who has clearly been assembled in a hurry in a cloak patched with pieces of other cloaks, guarding a teapot with their life. Dorcas is a Signpost Inspector and checks that every sign points at what it says and is, at present, three towns behind.

openObjectives.prompt: Dorcas has watched you walk past three times and has started to keep count. Tell Dorcas that you are lost, using Italian.
Dorcas is holding a map upside down and would rather be told. Tell Dorcas to turn left or right, using Italian.
Dorcas sits behind a small window from which things are evidently sold. Ask Dorcas for a ticket to somewhere, using Italian.

character.name: Dorcas Parsnip
character.description: A long-limbed figure who has clearly been assembled in a hurry in a cloak patched with pieces of other cloaks, guarding a teapot with their life. Dorcas is a Signpost Inspector and checks that every sign points at what it says and is, at present, three towns behind.

npc.narrative: It is notte at The Crooked Dell, and a light pioggia falls on a cartello that points two ways at once. Sotto it, a donna in a wet cappotto checks the legno against a list, then leaves a pause beside her, roughly successor-sized. Her lanterna gives a piccola luce.
npc.native: Buonasera! Sono Dorcas, e mi sono perso. E tu, ti sei perso?
npc.translation: Good evening! I am Dorcas, and I am lost. And you, are you lost?

player: Buonasera Dorcas. Si, mi sono perso. Dove è la stazione?

correction.text: Buonasera, Dorcas. Sì, mi sono perso. Dov'è la stazione?
correction.translation: Good evening, Dorcas. Yes, I am lost. Where is the station?

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice work: you greeted Dorcas, said you are lost, and even asked where the station is. Just watch the accent on \"Sì\" and the short form \"Dov'è\".

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you told Dorcas you are lost with "mi sono perso".
Here you are meant to tell Dorcas to turn left or right. Don't worry, it will come up again later.
Here you are meant to ask Dorcas for a ticket to somewhere. Don't worry, it will come up again later.

correction.text: Buonasera, Dorcas. Sì, mi sono perso. Dov'è la stazione?
correction.translation: Good evening, Dorcas. Yes, I am lost. Where is the station?

openObjectives.prompt: Dorcas is holding a map upside down and would rather be told. Tell Dorcas to turn left or right, using Italian.
Dorcas sits behind a small window from which things are evidently sold. Ask Dorcas for a ticket to somewhere, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Under a pioggia leggera, Dorcas holds a lanterna over her clipboard and counts something on her fingers. You join her at the crocevia, where due cartelli point with great confidence at the same siepe. Neither has been inspected, which she is writing down.
npc.native: Anche tu sei perso, bene! Non so dove è la stazione. Un segno dice: gira a sinistra. Un altro segno dice: a destra. Dove vado io?
npc.translation: You are lost too, good! I don't know where the station is. One sign says: turn left. Another sign says: right. Where do I go?

player: Gira a destra! Destra e bene, I think.

correction.text: Gira a destra! A destra è bene, penso.
correction.translation: Turn right! Right is good, I think.

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice work: you clearly told Dorcas to turn right, in good Italian. Just remember to put \"è\" with an accent, and the English bit can be said in Italian too.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: "Gira a destra" tells Dorcas to turn right.
Not yet: you still need to ask Dorcas for a ticket to somewhere. Don't worry, it will come up again later.

correction.text: Gira a destra! A destra è bene, penso.
correction.translation: Turn right! Right is good, I think.

openObjectives.prompt: Dorcas sits behind a small window from which things are evidently sold. Ask Dorcas for a ticket to somewhere, using Italian.

npc.narrative: In the notte, the pioggia drums on the segno, which points two ways with equal confidence. Dorcas ticks something off a list, then draws a damp bundle of stiff cards from her coat, each one stamped for a different città.
npc.native: Va bene, vado a destra! Io ho molti biglietti per le città. Dove vuoi andare tu?
npc.translation: All right, I am going right! I have many tickets for the cities. Where do you want to go?

player: Un biglietto per Roma, per favore.

verdict.overallFeedback: Great job! You asked politely for a ticket to Rome, and your Italian was clear and correct.

objectiveResults.feedback: You asked Dorcas for a ticket to Rome correctly in Italian.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: Un biglietto per Roma, per favore.

npc.narrative: Dorcas holds the lanterna high, and the pioggia makes the light wobble. A segno above the cancello is checked, then the carta, then the segno again. The carta loses, narrowly, and a wet timbro lands on your ticket.
npc.native: Un biglietto per Roma, per favore! Molto bene. Ecco il biglietto. Vai a Roma stasera?
npc.translation: A ticket for Rome, please! Very good. Here is the ticket. Are you going to Rome tonight?

player: Si, stasera. Dov'è il treno? A sinistra?

npc.narrative: Under the lampione, the pioggia taps softly on Dorcas's clipboard. She holds your biglietto up to the light, suspicious of it on principle. The signpost beside you points sinistra and destra with equal confidence, and neither has been checked.
npc.native: Stasera, bene! Non so dove è il treno. Uno: io vado a destra. Due: un segno dice treno. Vieni con me?
npc.translation: Tonight, good! I do not know where the train is. One: I go to the right. Two: a sign says train. Are you coming with me?

npc.narrative: You walk beside Dorcas along the strada, under a grey sky and a very black notte. She holds a lanterna in one hand and a pencil in the other, and every few steps she leaves a pause for somebody who is not there. Ahead, a segno leans as if it has heard something.
npc.native: Bene, andiamo! Uno: il segno dice treno. Due: io non credo al segno. E tu, credi al segno?
npc.translation: Good, let's go! One: the sign says train. Two: I do not believe the sign. And you, do you believe the sign?
